A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DualReal and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally contains Supplementary Section 7. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-customization comparisons, component and group-cardinality ablations in Tables 1–3, and qualitative and controller analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative outputs, a baseline comparison and an ablation example in Figures 8–11.

M1.justification: Dual-aware Adaptation, gradient masking, complementary adapter weighting and the StageBlender Controller remain unchanged. The supplementary training settings document the existing procedure rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions describe the same coverage: 50 identity subjects, 21 motion sequences and 50 prompts per case varying decoration or environment. The supplementary examples illustrate these customization requirements without establishing an expanded dataset or task.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain MotionBooth, LoRA, CogVideoX-5B full fine-tuning and DreamVideo. The additional qualitative comparison in Figure 10 uses this same set.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark setup, seven metrics and component-removal and group-cardinality evaluation designs are retained. Section 7.1 newly discloses training settings; it does not identify revisions to previously stated settings or a new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Section 7.3 and Figure 11 add a qualitative component ablation using a dog playing guitar with a floral crown under cherry branches. This supplements the existing gardener-prompt example while testing the same three component removals; the numerical ablations and controller analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the comparisons. The supplement introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 8–11 add customization outputs and qualitative comparison and ablation results. All numerical values in Tables 1–3 remain identical, including DualReal's CLIP-I of 0.629 and DINO-I of 0.551 in Table 1; the added examples support the existing qualitative findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same mathematical content. Explicitly writing the selector's binary domain and clarifying the parameter masks restates the existing formulation; no new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain adaptive joint identity-motion training, the two proposed components and the claimed average CLIP-I/DINO-I improvements of 21.7%/31.8%. Some passages replace 'lossless' with 'high-fidelity', but the title, abstract and contribution statements retain the original substantive claims.

C2.justification: Section 7.4 adds an applicability explanation asserting automatic adaptation from simple to intricate actions irrespective of input complexity. Existing interpretations of identity-motion conflicts, component effects and depth-dependent controller behavior remain, with no new limitations analysis.

D1.justification: New Section 7.1 supplies substantial implementation information absent from v1: DualReal's 1,000 training steps, 50% motion-training probability, AdamW, 1e-3 learning rate and 49-frame 480×720 outputs. It also documents baseline backbones, schedules, learning rates and batch sizes, plus LLM-based prompt expansion. The project-page address changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to CustomContrast, DSE-GAN, DQVAE and RealCustom++, and adds short discussions of DQVAE and RealCustom. The central positioning against isolated identity/motion customization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are retained. v2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, clarifies selector and mask descriptions, and adds acknowledgment and supplementary sections without extensively rewriting the paper.

P2.justification: Figures 8–11 substantially expand the visual presentation with condition/output grids, another baseline comparison and another component-ablation panel. Figures 1–7 are retained; Table 1 expands abbreviated metric headings, and the main text undergoes modest layout reflow.

improvement.justification: Section 7.1 improves experimental transparency by supplying previously missing training settings for DualReal and its baselines. Figures 8–11 provide useful additional qualitative support. The quantitative evidence remains unchanged, and the new input-complexity assertions lack a dedicated evaluation, so the overall gain is limited.
